notes: A table or guess-and-check earns L1 and L2 if it shows $11 per pizza and the $3 fee. L3 follows through: correctly solving 80 = (own price)·n + (own fee) earns it. A bare correct answer earns L3 only.
Each student gets 6 cups of sugar. Units are not required.
Each student gets 5 cups of flour. Accept 7 1/2 and 15/2. Units are not required.
The dollar sign is not required.

lines.description: Plots the two points from part a in the right places: (20, 1500) and (50, 3000), or the student's own part-a values.
Draws one straight line through those points that reaches the vertical axis (at 500 with the correct values).

notes: Follow-through: points and a line built from the student's own wrong part-a answers earn every line. A sketch on the student's own axes is fine as long as the scale makes the positions readable.

lines.description: Slope is 50, or the slope of the student's own line from part b.
Explains the slope as $50 (or their slope) per hour of labor.

notes: L2 needs both the rate and the per-hour meaning; "the cost" alone is not enough.

lines.description: Finds the intercept 4, or the correct intercept for the student's own slope through (2, 5) or (6, 7).
Writes an equation of the line: y = 1/2 x + 4 or an equivalent form.

notes: Accept y = 0.5x + 4, y − 5 = 1/2(x − 2), y − 7 = 1/2(x − 6) and x − 2y = −8. Point-slope form with the right slope earns L2 and L3 without computing the intercept.

lines.description: Gives both distances: Tyler about 1.2 miles, Elena about 1.18 miles (10 ÷ 8.5).

notes: The difference is read from a graph, so accept any reasoned estimate (Kincaid confirmed): about 0.02 or 0.03 miles, or 2/85 mile.
Accept 25/3 and about 8.33 for Tyler. Units are not required.

lines.description: Picks the runner with fewer minutes per mile in the student's own part b (Tyler, with the correct paces).
Reasons that fewer minutes per mile is faster, comparing the paces.

notes: Follow-through: a student whose part-b paces are wrong earns both lines by picking the runner with fewer minutes per mile in their own work and saying why. Naming Tyler while the student's own paces favor Elena does not earn L1.

lines.description: Interprets it as the cost of each class, $20.
Interprets it as the $60 membership fee to join (the cost with zero classes).

notes: "It costs $60 to join" earns both lines.

lines.description: Uses a rate of 3 inches per month.
Uses a starting height of 12 inches, giving h = 3t + 12.

notes: Accept h = 12 + 3t. Using t and h swapped (t = 3h + 12) loses L2.

lines.description: Sets up 66 = 3t + 12, or the student's own equation from part a with h = 66.
18 months, or the correct solution of the student's own equation.

notes: Follow-through: a wrong part-a equation solved correctly for h = 66 earns both lines.
